challenges.name: promise-combinators-dashboard-quiz
challenges.title: What does the dashboard do when one service fails?
challenges.description: Predict how Promise.all and its siblings behave on the account dashboard before you read on.

questions.question:
The dashboard runs:

const [profile, loyalty, activity, offers] = await Promise.all([
  getProfile(),   // resolves after 120 ms
  getLoyalty(),   // resolves after 300 ms
  getActivity(),  // resolves after 450 ms
  getOffers(),    // rejects with HTTP 500 after 80 ms
]);

What happens?
questions.explanation: Promise.all rejects with the first rejection it sees - here the offers error at 80 ms - and the await throws. The other three requests are not cancelled: promises are not cancellable, so the fetches keep running and their results are simply discarded. The dashboard throws away three good responses because of one optional widget.

options.text: At 80 ms the await throws the offers error. The other three requests keep running, but their results are discarded.
At 80 ms the await throws, and Promise.all cancels the three requests that are still running.
At 450 ms the await resolves with offers set to undefined.
At 450 ms the await throws an AggregateError that contains only the offers error.

questions.question: Static assets are served from three CDN mirrors. You want the first mirror that answers SUCCESSFULLY and want to ignore mirrors that fail. One mirror is down and rejects after 5 ms; the others answer after 40 ms and 70 ms. Which call gives you the 40 ms response?
questions.explanation: Promise.any resolves with the first fulfilled promise and only rejects - with an AggregateError holding every reason - when all of them fail. Promise.race settles with whichever promise settles first, success or failure, so it would reject at 5 ms with the dead mirror's error. Promise.all would also reject at 5 ms, and Promise.allSettled waits for all three (70 ms) and never picks a winner for you.

challenges.name: load-dashboard-required-optional-timeouts
challenges.title: Load the dashboard: required vs optional sources with timeouts
challenges.description: Write loadDashboard(sources, timers). All sources load in parallel; each can have its own timeout. A failed or timed-out optional source falls back and is reported in errors, a failed required source rejects the dashboard immediately, and no timer outlives a resolved dashboard. The tests replay every source on a fake clock and compare when and how the dashboard settles.

tests.name: All four services healthy: the dashboard renders when the slowest one answers
Offers returns HTTP 500: the dashboard still renders, with the fallback
A 9-second activity feed is cut off at its 1.5 s timeout
A failed required source rejects at once, without waiting for slow optional ones
A broken optional client and a hung request: both fall back, timers are cleaned up
